title: Register the line-break collapse of edge-glyph dependence (edge_gap) and attack it with a line-restarting glyph chain
statement: Work on K-002-open-2, public training pages only (192 pages, paragraph text, certain words, identical line widths and word counts for the synthetic text). Boundary statistics, shuffle-corrected at matched pair counts: the manuscript has 0.198 bits of dependence between a word's last glyph and the next word's first glyph within lines (25,796 pairs) and 0.002 bits across line breaks (2,765 pairs, paragraph starts excluded). With uncertain spaces joined instead of split the figures are 0.164 and 0.004, so the collapse does not depend on how uncertain separators are read; the within-line level does (about 17% lower). Spacing statistics: word length in glyphs has mean 4.48, sd 1.65 (4.81, 1.72 joined). One fixed procedure fitted on the same pages, a glyph chain of order 4 inside the word whose first glyph is drawn given the last glyph of the word before and which starts afresh at each line from the line-initial distribution, gives 0.197 within lines, 0.007 across breaks, length mean 4.49, sd 1.77, 6,770 types and hapax share 0.66 at 32,410 words (manuscript 7,042 and 0.69 at 32,142). The same chain run straight through line breaks keeps 0.198 bits across them, so the collapse needs a writer who treats the line as a unit; the repository's self-citation generator gives 0.021 within and 0.014 across. So on public pages the answer is yes for the boundary statistics and close for spacing (the chain's lengths are a little too spread). None of this is scored yet: the measurement language cannot state the collapse. Proposed step: once the statistic edge_gap (branch code-L2-edge-gap-fleet-fable) is merged, register the fact {"select": {"unit": ["P"], "certain": true}, "statistic": {"edge_gap": true}, "compare": [{"op": ">=", "value": 0.08}, {"null": "shuffle_within_page", "direction": "greater", "perms": 199, "p": 0.01}]} (practice split: 0.198 ZL, 0.154 Takahashi, 0.166 RF, p 0.005 each), then attack it. A blind word stream cannot restart at hidden line starts, so the attack also needs a line-aware attack form (branch code-R-line-aware-attack-fleet-fable covers line ends; line starts would need the same).
check: fact.json with the edge_gap spec above, scored once on the hidden pages and on Takahashi; then attack.json against it with text from a line-restarting glyph chain fitted on public pages only.
